data.narrative:
Ohalo Genetics is a Series C-stage biotech company that has raised $205M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer universe of 3 public-market comps (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private-market precedents in Biotech & Health, with particular relevance to same-stage peers including Colossal Biosciences ($10.3B), Chai Discovery ($3.8B), and New Limit ($3.1B).

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-Progression anchors to the $205M total capital raised and applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $348M. Peer-Median triangulation uses the median valuation across the three same-sector, same-stage comparables, producing $3.8B; the range among these peers spans $3.1B to $10.3B. Public-Comp Anchoring cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure, which is standard for private companies. The public biotech sector median P/S stands at 7.4x across the three public tickers.

The two applicable methods produce a wide triangulated range: low of $296M, median of $2.1B, and high of $4.4B. The substantial spread reflects the dispersion within the peer set—particularly the $10.3B outlier (Colossal)—and methodological divergence between capital-efficiency and peer-median approaches. Key uncertainties include whether Ohalo's technical differentiation and clinical pipeline justify positioning toward the higher end of peer valuations or whether stage-adjusted capital metrics better reflect risk profile.
